title: Welcome
elements: Introduces device-hosted sharing; it is explanatory text, not a control.
Direct Sharing / Secure Tunnels / Your Device
Completes onboarding and opens Home. Onboarding does not repeat on the next launch.

title: Home: Send Files
elements: Shows detected network information. The fixture uses 192.168.1.42; native testing used the emulator's 10.0.2.15. The pill no longer invents an IP or pretends a server is already listening.
Changes the selected task. Receive clears selected send files. Receive to Room now switches correctly; navigating between bottom tabs preserves the current selection.
Explains browser-based sharing. Select Files / Folder opens the file selector; with selected items it shows their count and Edit.
Enables password protection and opens the security sheet. A password must actually be configured before launch; cancelling an empty setup no longer creates an effectively open room.
Send-only vault control. It now sets an explicit limit of one download per file. It is disabled with an explanation in Receive and Room modes.
Opens the provider selector, including configured providers and their setup dialogs.
Local disables public tunnelling; Cloudflare selects Quick Tunnel; Auto chooses automatic provider selection. Other custom providers do not falsely highlight Cloudflare.
Starts the server for the selected files. Missing files produce an error; a PIN-enabled session without a configured password opens security setup. Repeated starts are disabled while starting.
Explains what launch produces and displays a start failure when present. Scroll if the action is below the floating navigation bar.
Home, Received, Transfers, History and Settings. Tap or drag across the bar. Tabs keep their local filter and mode state; inactive animations are disabled. Repeated drags now reset correctly.

title: Home: Receive Mode
elements: Animated receiving illustration, not transfer progress.
Refers to the configured receive folder. The fabricated 48.2 GB free figure and progress bar were removed.
PIN and tunnel choices work as on Home. One-time downloads is explicitly unavailable because this screen accepts uploads.
Starts the upload server. Verified with a real 58-byte test upload; the Received list refreshed and /api/files remained empty.

title: Home: Room
elements: Introduces temporary rooms. Messages remain in memory; media uses temporary private cache.
Writes the actual session expiry. Previously this changed only the highlight, and 24 hr was displayed despite the room engine supporting at most two hours.
PIN and reach configure the room. One-time download limits are a Send Files feature.
Opens room configuration. Local connection choice is now preserved on entering room setup.

title: File selector
elements: Return to Home. Selection is managed in the session provider.
Filters the selected items; it does not scan all storage.
Opens the Android file picker. The picker and its media-permission handoff were exercised.
Opens folder selection. A real folder selection was not completed in this review.
Shows chosen items with type and size; removal changes the share selection.
Summary of selected items, not free disk capacity.
Returns with the selected files. Disabled when there are no items.

title: Live sharing / receiving
elements: Encodes the currently selected interface URL. Tap for the fullscreen QR view.
Select the URL appropriate to the interface. Tunnel states include connecting, failed/retry and available.
Switches between detected interface addresses. The emulator exposes 10.0.2.15 and 10.0.2.16; those are emulator addresses, not this computer's LAN address.
Shows the same target as the QR. The browser hint explains typing http:// for local sharing.
Opens the OS share sheet. No recipient was selected or message sent.
Launches the URL in a browser. Browser inspection was blocked by the browser-origin permission gate and was not worked around.
People / MB/s / MB sent or received
Live server counters. These are observational counters, not benchmark guarantees.
Stops the session and its tunnel. Native Receive stop was verified. The current implementation stops directly after its exit animation.

title: Fullscreen connection QR
elements: Larger scan target for the selected connection URL.
Dismisses the view. The brightness override is restored after dismissal.

title: Tunnel failure
elements: Explains that public allocation failed while the local server remains available.
Calls the tunnel retry action; covered by an existing widget test.
Allow continuing with an available local interface.

title: Received files
elements: Total bytes in files scanned from the receive folder. Removed the fictitious 64 GB capacity and minimum 5% usage bar.
Counts the receive folder, not just today's files. The label now matches that scope.
Type badge, filename, size and modified-time label. Tapping opens the file through its associated app.
Open, Share and Delete actions. Delete has a confirmation. No personal file was opened, shared or deleted.
Rescans the configured folder. Upload completion also triggers refresh.
Explains that no received files match the list or filter.

title: Transfers: empty and filters
elements: Screen title and server-reported aggregate throughput.

title: Transfers: active
elements: Fraction transferred; completed records show Done.
Estimated from current throughput. The test source was deliberately throttled; the values are not performance benchmarks.
Now controls the server's actual transfer wait rather than only changing the UI record.
Now cancels the server stream, wakes paused waits and marks the record terminal.

title: Transfers: pause verified
elements: The same upload remained at 40.9 MB across two observations, with throughput dropping to zero.
Can terminate a paused transfer without resuming it first.

title: Transfers: cancelled
elements: Terminal record with no further pause/cancel controls. Other failures are labelled Failed.
The test client observed ECONNRESET. Android storage inspection showed no incomplete fixture file.
The earlier 58-byte test upload completed successfully.

title: History
elements: Shows persisted completed file-sharing session records.
No qualifying past Send session has been recorded. Receive-only sessions are not currently added by stopServer; rooms do not persist chat history.
When present, show session date, selected-item count, transferred bytes, duration and security label.
Remove a record or confirm clearing all records. No existing history was removed during this review.

title: Settings: device and appearance
elements: Opens Edit Device Name. Save persists a name; Cancel dismisses without applying it.
Informational preferred port, 8080; it is not an editable input. The live connection URL carries the actual bound port.
Opens folder selection for incoming files and shows the current destination.
Local Wi-Fi only, Cloudflare tunnel, or Bore relay defaults. A custom Bore choice may open its configuration sheet.

title: Edit device name
elements: Dismiss without change, or save and close.

title: Settings: background and diagnostics
elements: Reports the foreground service. Fix starts it only when a session is active; idle status does not mean a sharing session is broken.
Reports battery-optimization exemption and can open the corresponding Android flow.
Reports the native watchdog state and offers its recovery flow.
Runs the background-permission and OEM assistance flow. OEM-specific behavior was not verified on physical hardware.
Opens the in-memory diagnostic log viewer.
Opens custom-domain setup. Live provisioning requires user credentials and was not attempted.

title: Diagnostic logs
elements: Opens sharing for the log export. No export was sent.
Drag/dismiss the sheet or use its surrounding scrim.

title: Cloudflare setup
elements: Names the setup task and dismisses the sheet.
Opens the Cloudflare tab of Tunnel Setup Guide.
Sensitive input with reveal/hide and paste buttons. Their containing width now fits both buttons; the native review reproduced a 52-pixel overflow before this fix.
Optional account selection hint, with a paste button.
Enabled when a token is present; fetches authorized accounts/zones.
Appear after fetching zones and automate tunnel/DNS setup. Not exercised against a real account.

title: Bore relay setup
elements: Opens the Custom Bore VPS help tab.
Relay configuration. The default control port is 7835.
Validates and saves the relay choice.
Bore uses plaintext transport; no speed or confidentiality guarantee is established by this review.

title: Tunnel guide
elements: Relay deployment and firewall instructions. Third-party cost/speed claims in this help text were not independently verified.
Read the selected guide and dismiss it. No external account or VPS configuration was performed.

title: Room: host setup
elements: Returns to Home and clears room configuration mode; Send cannot accidentally start as a room after exiting setup.
Description of the room's intended temporary lifecycle. Attachments use private cache rather than RAM only.
Shows local-only or the selected public provider. A local choice from Home is now preserved.
Opens supported durations. Defaults longer than the engine's two-hour room limit are normalized before presentation.
Displayed for Cloudflare Quick when applicable. Its Settings action opens Android hotspot settings.
Starts the configured room. Empty required PIN configuration is rejected before launch.

title: Room timer sheet
elements: Sets the actual expiry and closes the sheet. Unsupported six- and 24-hour room choices were removed.
The authoritative countdown starts on the first successful join; it is not extended from this sheet once live.
The sheet is scrollable and no longer overflows at a phone-sized viewport.

title: Room security sheet
elements: Appears when enabled; changes the configured password and can reveal or obscure its display.
Closes the sheet. A required but missing password cannot silently authorize joins.

title: Room: join setup
elements: Accepts a full invite URL or dynamic Chat ID. Chat ID resolution now requires a PIN and never downloads an invite token from public discovery.
Parses a copied room link and fills its supplied details.
PIN required for Chat ID joins and for PIN-protected full links; eye toggles obscuring.
Validates input, resolves a Chat ID if needed and opens the native room chat.

title: QR scanner
elements: Aims the camera at a CloudPocket QR. The emulator's synthetic camera preview opened successfully; decoding a physical QR was not verified.
Toggles the camera torch where supported.
Allows connecting from a copied link.
Explains invalid or untrusted QR contents, or offers app settings and clipboard fallback if camera access fails.

title: Live room
elements: Room status presentation. The badge is not proof that relays cannot obtain admission key material; see the security limitations below.
Remaining lifetime and progress; pending-first-join state is separate from the authoritative running countdown.
Copies the dynamic code when useful. The caption explains that Chat ID joins need a PIN; token-only rooms use invite links.
Displays/copies the host-configured PIN where present. These screenshots contain fixtures, not user credentials.
Opens the invitation sheet, including QR/link sharing and browser-password options.
Joins the host chat with its room token and PIN. Previously token-only hosts omitted their own token.
Confirms ending the room, disconnecting participants, clearing chat RAM and unlinking cached media. It does not securely shred flash storage.

title: Native chat
elements: Returns to the room dashboard. Closing chat no longer leaves asynchronous callbacks calling setState on a disposed screen.
Uses the server's roomCode and remainingSeconds fields.
Loads the server's messages history and distinguishes text, system and media envelopes. A real local connection verified the rendered history fixture.
Selects supported room media and streams an upload. Native requests now include room credentials for protected media endpoints.
Sends typed text, using AES-GCM payload encryption when a room secret is available.
Opens the private viewer. Returning restores the chat's screenshot guard.

title: Private media viewer
evidence: Flutter-rendered fixture; Android capture guard retained
elements: Identifies the media and explains the in-app viewing policy.
Displays a bounded text preview. The screenshot uses a small synthetic text fixture.
The same screen selects image preview, page navigation or native player controls by media type. Native codec/PDF playback was not exercised on a physical ARM64 device.
Closes the view and removes temporary viewer copies where created. It does not promise secure flash erasure.
Native guarded screens were not captured or modified to bypass FLAG_SECURE. The image is from Flutter's test renderer, not an Android screenshot of protected content.
